title: DVR quotient augmentation, Koszul completion and open completeness
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], $B_{n,T}=(A_n)_T$ and $\widehat R_T=\lim_nB_{n,T}$. Use the strict semilinear module-system category $\mathscr S_T$, derived reduction $\mathcal R_T\dashv\mathcal L_T$, and the actual unit $u$ and counit $e$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Completeness means the quotient-tower Roos-triangle condition of [def-weil-derived-complete], and normalized means that every transition-adjoint $N_m\otimes^L_{B_{m,T}}B_{n,T}\to N_n$ is invertible for $m\ge n$.

The pair $(R,(t))$ satisfies [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]: $R$ is Noetherian, $R/(t)$ is additive torsion, and each $A_n$ is finite and perfect over $R$, with finite-free resolution $[R\xrightarrow{t^n}R]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$. The canonical constant-sheaf comparison identifies $B_{n,T}$ with the sheafification of $V\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|V|),A_n)$, including all quotient maps; its limit identifies $\widehat R_T$ with the sheaf $A_T$ of that datum [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction].

For every $P\in D(\widehat R_T)$, the strict quotient tower $P_\bullet$ of that datum is canonically the scalar restriction $U_T\mathcal R_TP$, and the canonical quotient completion map is the actual adjunction unit:
$$\operatorname{comp}_P=u_P:P\longrightarrow\mathcal L_T\mathcal R_TP.$$
On a single flat-term K-flat representative $Q$, the two maps have the same simultaneous representative: the strict augmentation from the constant tower $\Delta Q$, with components $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, before total derived limit [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. For the intrinsic Koszul completion $P^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}}$, its map $\kappa_P$, and the specified comparison $c_P$ [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion, prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction], one has
$$c_P\circ\kappa_P=u_P.$$
Quotient-tower completeness of $P$ is equivalent to invertibility of $\kappa_P$.

For every quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], localized extension by zero $j_!$ [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] sends every quotient-complete $K\in D(\widehat R_U)$ to a quotient-complete $j_!K$. The actual unit $u_{j_!K}=\operatorname{comp}_{j_!K}$ is invertible, and its composite with the total-limit Roos projection is the actual reduction map at each $n$. No boundedness, constructibility, finite-type hypothesis on the schemes, or commutation of $j_!$ with arbitrary inverse limits is assumed.

proof.text: The already proved principalKoszulStrictReplacement.coefficient_datum supplies the datum. Multiplication by a nonzero power of the DVR uniformizer has cokernel the prescribed quotient. Apply the mapping-cone short-exact-complex quasi-isomorphism and the single-complex bounds; cone terms are sums of two finite free terms.

Construct finite constant-to-function comparisons by sheafification, normalize them on constants and verify quotient transitions there by local surjectivity. Take the isomorphism of whole inverse diagrams and its limit. Restrict scalars along the canonical ring isomorphism to obtain the coefficient equivalence. Construct open coefficient restriction by continuous/cocontinuous sheafification compatibility, and its completed comparison by preservation of limits; actual open extension is the normalized exact adjoint.

The augmented-tower comparison supplies tower, rlim, limit_model, representative and actual-unit fields. The specified koszulReconstruction comparison gives koszul_unit by associativity. Compose the intrinsic comparison equation with its inverse to give intrinsic_unit. The intrinsic criterion supplies complete_iff.

Use the intrinsic criterion on U, intrinsic open transport, then the criterion on X to obtain quotient completeness. The intrinsic-unit equation expresses the mapped actual calculus unit as the intrinsic unit followed by isomorphisms. An equivalence reflects isomorphisms, giving actual-unit invertibility. The calculus unit_projection field is exactly the required final finite projection equation.
